However, turning to the advocacy effort in the Middle East on economic, social, and cultural rights, our center worked on a number of important practical matters. I would like to give some examples. Turning to refugees' rights and education, the organization supported small initiatives for Syrian refugees, including the education of the youth and children affected by conflict. We believe that the right to education, especially for children and refugees, is part and parcel of the social, economic, and cultural rights. One of the latest programs was a grant worth $550 to Yesar in Hatay to provide Syrian youth with the necessary school equipment. And our online website, Lebanon allowed us to support Mohammed Jindi, who is a student who was awarded from the EU for refugee creativities. Turning to socioeconomic inclusion, our center in 2018 supported members of the Syrian refugees under the umbrella of the Syrian Dares Club, who have presented their stories before Americans here in New York, New Jersey, and other states. They have also tried to present some of the cultural aspects, including food, culture, and other matters to present their cultural identity and convey their experience to a wider community. Turning to education and cultural rights of refugees, in 2019, the center launched Music for Refugees initiative, which focused on a Syrian refugee in Turkey called Samah Hajazi. She assisted dozens of children to learn music for For us, this is a clear example that education and, and culture is not a luxury. However, we have to support them psychologically and uphold their right for creativity and education. During COVID-19, we launched awareness campaigns for a number of refugee children with the presence of specialized doctors in the United States via Zoom. They are also present on our online website. In Arabic. We could not provide full English translation. However, they are present. Turning to social protection and the protection of children's rights, in 2020 we provided some material on sexual violence that a child in Lebanon have been subjected to, and we tried to ensure the prosecution of the perpetrators to ensure social protection. This is one of the approaches adopted by the Center to uphold socioeconomic and cultural rights in terms of vulnerabilities and displacement, to respond to crises and ensure the right to housing and decent life. In February 2023, the center launched some material on the Syrian and Turkish earthquakes. We clarified the volume of damage materially and in kind. And we cooperated with some NGOs where we called for help to Turkish and Syrian people and to provide the support to everyone. All of it is present in our online website. You can easily access them. Turning to the right to education and decent work and social justice, the center has launched a number of articles and media material to address food security, meet inflation, the provision of potable water, agriculture, to uphold socioeconomic rights that are relevant to the daily life of people so that they can have a decent living. And turning to agriculture and rural life, today we have sent to the— our colleague, the Turkish ambassador, or the Turkish delegate, a letter to be conveyed to the Turkish mission. The main aim of the letter is to address the problem of flooding, especially in Deir ez-Zor in Syria. The objective was to convey the impact of such flooding on the agricultural land farmers and others. This is a clear example that our advocacy is not based on a confrontation with governments. Instead, we try to convey the life on the ground and to uphold the socioeconomic rights of people through drawing a real picture. Turning to cultural rights and protecting civil and the artistic landscape, we supported so many initiatives, the last of which was the Bustan Project.
